name: Freeway Park
note: Cost from Wikipedia only (unverified by a primary source). Funding was a mix of federal and state highway funds plus city Forward Thrust bond money; split not found. Original 1976 lid ~4.5 ac (HistoryLink); later expansions brought the park to ~5.2 ac, so cost/acre understates 1976 unit cost. The Urbanist (2015) cites ~$18M/acre for Freeway Park and Aubrey Davis lid (basis unclear).

name: I-579 Cap / Frankie Pace Park
note: Final cost ~$32M (FHWA; other reports $30-32.3M; initial estimate $26.4M). Federal = FY2016 TIGER grant ($19M in most reports, $20M per FHWA). State = RACP $5.23M + PennDOT Multimodal $0.65M + CFA $1.35M + DCNR Keystone $0.5M. FHWA: $12M from state, local and private sources plus a land match. Ribbon cutting Nov 22, 2021.

name: Klyde Warren Park
note: Federal = ARRA stimulus; state = TxDOT highway funds; local = city bond; private = '$50M+'. Listed sources sum to ~$106.7M of $110M budget. Park now cites 5.4 acres. O&M (~$2M/yr) privately raised plus a PID.

name: Margaret T. Hance Park (Deck Park Tunnel)
note: acres = deck area (13 ac of the 30-32 ac park sits on 19 side-by-side bridges). Cost = tunnel structure $55M + electrical/mechanical $20M (FHWA); excludes park landscaping. Built as a state-city-federal partnership; split not given. Later: $8.6M Fiesta Bowl PLAY playground ($2M Fiesta Bowl, rest city parks initiative); park master plan estimated $80-118M.

name: The Cap at Union Station
note: Retail cap (25,500 sq ft of shops), not a park. cost_usd = sum of reported components: $7.8M private retail + $1.625M cap platforms/utility connections + $115K design. State = ODOT platforms; local = city title/design/utilities; private = Continental Real Estate ($7.0M loan, $0.3M mezzanine, $0.5M equity). City leases platforms for $1/yr plus 10% of profit. Platforms were built during the federally aided I-670 High St bridge work (federal share not itemized).

name: Capitol Crossing (I-395 air-rights deck)
note: Development platform with streets/plazas, not a park. $263.3M = deck/infrastructure package (ENR 2020); full mixed-use development ~$1.3B. Developer Property Group Partners bought air rights (2012-13) and financed the work; public/private split not published in sources found. Year = ENR Project of the Year (Oct 2020); exact completion not confirmed.

name: Central 70 Cover Park
note: $125M per High Country News; unclear whether lid structure + park or park only. Part of the $1.2B Central 70 project (CDOT also cites $1.3B), funded by CDOT Bridge Enterprise, DRCOG, SB 228 and City of Denver. Opened Nov 30, 2022 next to Swansea Elementary. 56 households displaced for cover and added lanes.

name: Fort Washington Way Cap
note: 2023 RCN construction application ($149.8M request, $37.5M local match) was not funded. Jul 2026: $25M federal grant for final design/construction of first stage (Vine to Walnut); city and county must each find $12M match; no schedule set.

name: HUB404 (Park Over GA 400)
note: Stalled: original 2025 opening missed; latest found reporting (~2022) put completion ~2030 if funded. No 2024-2026 status confirmed; treat as stalled/possibly cancelled. Earlier estimates $190-250M; 7.1-9.1 ac. Federal = $750K appropriation. Led by Buckhead CID and HUB404 Conservancy.

name: Halperin Park (formerly Southern Gateway Deck Park)
note: Phase 1 (2.8 ac) opened May 9, 2026; Phase 2 (to ~5 ac) still under way, so acres/cost are full-program figures. Cost: ~$300M full public-private program (Halperin Park site, GT Law); foundation's earlier fast-facts put Phase 1 at $112M; FHWA profile listed Phase 1 at $82M. State = TxDOT deck/structure. Local = city bond $7.1M (FHWA) plus up to $8M more approved 2026. Private = $23M Halperin Foundation naming gift; FHWA profile also lists $35M philanthropic and $40M from NCTCOG (regional transportation funds, origin not specified). ~$200M of $300M reported secured.

name: I-35 Caps and Stitches (Our Future 35)
note: Only foundations are funded: May 2025 council committed ~$104M ($41M State Infrastructure Bank loan + $63M certificates of obligation) for supports under 3 downtown caps (Cesar Chavez-4th, 4th-7th, 11th-12th) and 2 northern stitches. Decks/amenities unfunded; council decision due Nov 2026 (staff floated up to $750M debt). Lost $105M federal grant for Cesar Chavez-4th cap. acres/cost = original 8-site vision (>26 ac; ~$284M roadway + ~$600M caps, before amenities); later estimates >30 ac / >$800M.

name: Klyde Warren Park expansion (Klyde Warren 2.0)
note: Current mix per park (Jun 2026): City of Dallas (2024 bond), NCTCOG, Regional Transportation Council, Dallas County, KWP/Arts District PID, philanthropy; amounts not published. local/private figures ($10M city bond, $20M donor) are from the earlier ~$65M plan (HR&A page). Cost reports conflict: ~$121M (NBC/D Magazine, Jun 2026) vs Axios $96-111M construction + ~$80M amenities vs 'nearly $200M' (Fox 4). TxDOT awarded deck contract to Archer Western; construction to start before end of 2026, ~24 months; completion reported as late 2028 or 2029.

name: Lid I-5
note: 2020 feasibility study (WSP/OPCD), Madison St to Denny Way: 17-ac test area; $966M (park lid) to ~$2.5B (development lid), 'very preliminary', excludes many factors; 2.5-9.8 ac of new park possible. Study paid by $1.5M WSCC expansion community-benefits package; $2.2M federal+state planning (2024). City visioning 2026-2028; no design or construction funding.

name: Penn's Landing I-95 Cap Park
note: Pledges were made against the 2017 $225M estimate; cost now $329M (WHYY cites >$350M for broader effort), so the split does not cover the current total. State = PennDOT ($100M per Next City/Billy Penn; CBS says $110M; federal-aid share not itemized). Local = City of Philadelphia. Private = William Penn Foundation (up to $15M). ~12 ac park, of which roughly a third is on the new cap. Steel deck beams set Feb-Nov 2026; full completion now expected 2029 (older 2026 targets obsolete).

name: Rondo Community Land Bridge
note: Cost '>$450M' for structure only (estimate); 15-21 ac of new land. State = 2021 legislative appropriation for development; federal = Reconnecting Communities planning grant. Depends on MnDOT 'Rethinking I-94' alternative (no preferred alternative as of latest reporting). 2025 bill HF 494 to bar state spending was laid over (outcome not found).

name: Roy Blunt Luminary Park (South Loop Link)
note: Phase 1 (Block One, Wyandotte to Baltimore; 1 of 4 blocks) funded Sept 2026 at >$164M; construction from winter 2026-27, I-670 lane closures Dec 2026-Sep 2028, completion spring 2029. cost_usd = $164M + 3 x ~$60M per remaining block (KCUR) - arithmetic on reported figures, full build unfunded. Federal = ~$28M secured by Sen. Blunt; 2024 council approval cited $57M state+federal; $75M federal RCN application failed. Mix includes city, MoDOT and philanthropy (amounts not published). Missed 2026 World Cup target.

name: The Stitch
note: Full build 14 ac / >$700M over 3 phases (~2036 if funded). Phase 1 retooled Oct 2025 to ~5 ac (was 5.7 ac, ~$200M). Federal: $157.6M Reconnecting Communities grant (2024), of which $151.4M was rescinded by the 2025 reconciliation act. Local: $50M secured for design and the Stitch Special Services District (approved Apr 2025, funds O&M). Phase 1 targeted shovel-ready by mid-2026; no groundbreaking found.
